extra.frozen_placement: Base cache is generic support + transferred R. Only result-region keys and/or values are replaced by the fresh-R tensors computed after that same support. Support, prefix and separator tensors, token IDs, packed positions, masks, cursor, prompts and greedy decoding are identical. Keys are copied as stored; no RoPE is applied again.
extra.scope: Implementation and timing comparison. Dev sheets were already used for checkpoint selection; eval sheets were already used for the candidate's evaluation and are reused here as timing inputs. Neither is a new independent confirmation.
extra.timing_note: Single T4, A and B on the same GPU. Sender preparation runs on A's GPU-resident cache; movement is the host-to-GPU copy of what B receives (network transfer not modelled; bytes reported). Public support (KV) and the public text header are prefilled once and kept on B's GPU; their one-time cost is reported separately. Every condition prefills the prompt tokens shared by its plan and answer passes once.

protocol.question: Once the frozen query adapter is merged into B's q_proj weights, is the adapted compact-KV handoff still as reliable, and is it repeatably cheaper than text when the whole handoff is timed fairly?
protocol.scope: Implementation and timing comparison only. No training. Dev sheets were already used for checkpoint selection and eval sheets for the candidate's evaluation; both are reused here and neither counts as a new independent confirmation.

frozen.candidate: results_stage_plan4_qadapt/frozen_candidate.json (epoch 1, sha256 864a8f19...); the run refuses a changed checkpoint
unchanged: selected states (tk_tv, fk_fv, full KV) built by the qadapt prep code
decoding allowances 384 plan / 48 answer, greedy, thinking off, eager attention, fp16

merge.rule: W_merged = fp16(W.float() + scale * B.float() @ A.float()), scale = alpha / rank = 2, rounded once
merge.receiver_only: merged tensors are stored beside the original weights and swapped in only for B's own forwards; A, support construction and every baseline use the original weights, verified by a byte digest and wrapper identity before and after each phase
rounding_reported: rounding error relative to the fp32 update
cosine between the applied and fp32 update

agreement_dev.compare: unmerged (evaluated candidate) vs merged: forced logits on the unmerged outputs (plan and answer), generated eligibility labels, final choices and formatting; the unmerged rerun is also compared with the saved dev rows

gates.formatting: no more parse failures, truncations or missing plan lines than unmerged

agreement_dev.reporting: every sheet whose merged output differs is listed with the carriers that changed, whether or not the gates pass

bench.sheets: plan4_qadapt_eval, all 48 (reused inputs, labelled as a timing comparison)

conditions.merged_kv: compact support + R, merged receiver (the candidate after merging)
conditions.unmerged_kv: same cache, unmerged adapter (the evaluated candidate)
conditions.fk_fv: reconstruction: public support + R token IDs prefilled by B, original weights
conditions.text_result: R decoded to text and read as a message, original weights

bench.order: condition order shuffled per sheet and repetition (seeded 2026)
bench.warm_up: one discarded handoff per condition on the first sheet of each process
components: sender preparation (GPU gather + RoPE re-rotation of R; text: decode R tokens; reconstruction: token IDs)
movement (host-to-GPU copy of what B receives; bytes reported; network not modelled)
fairness: public support is prefilled once per template and kept on B's GPU; its one-time cost is reported separately
text gets the equivalent reuse: its public prompt header, cut strictly before the message, is prefilled once across sheets
every condition prefills the prompt tokens shared by its plan and answer prompts once per sheet and crops back between passes
generation uses the frozen R; the timed sender output is discarded after an untimed per-sheet check against it
bench.statistics: per sheet median over repetitions, family-level cluster bootstrap (2000 draws, seed 2026) on merged minus each comparison, plus the mean difference within each repetition
bench.reliability_check: merged vs unmerged in the bench (repetition 1): at most 2 of 576 labels, 2 all-twelve cases and 2 final choices lost

decision_rule.useful_practical_result: reliability check passes AND merged minus text complete handoff time has a 95% CI upper bound below zero AND every repetition's mean difference is below zero
decision_rule.otherwise: report the limit, with the preparation, prefill and decode differences that explain it
decision_rule.break_even: one-time adapter cost (teacher targets, training state build, training, merge) divided by the per-handoff saving, only if the saving is repeatable
decision_rule.not_claimed: superiority of the communication format: the KV receiver was adapted and the text receiver was not

protocol.textadapt_diagnostic: the frozen adapter (unmerged) applied to the text receiver on the eval sheets; a negative result would not show what a separately text-trained receiver could achieve
